newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan electronics output seen rising 5.3% in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Japan electronics output seen rising 5.3% in 1997.

text.p: Japanese production of electronics products is expected to increase 5.3 percent in calendar 1997, aided by an estimated 14.8 percent growth in computer production, an industry body said on Friday.

High levels of investment related to information products and the introduction of new personal computer operating systems and equipment will buoy production of computer terminals, the Electronic Industries Association of Japan (EIAJ) said.
But it saw production rises in communications equipment such as cell phones at a minimal 1.3 percent next year, against a gain of an estimated 31 percent in 1996.
Production of components and devices such as semiconductors and liquid crystal displays is forecast to grow 3.4 percent, after an estimated decline of 1.0 percent in 1996.

In consumer electrical appliances, where output fell for the fifth year in a row in 1996, introduction of new products such as digital video disc players (DVD), digital video cameras and mini disc players is expected to lift production by 2.1 percent in 1997, EIAJ said.
An increase in imports will continue in high-tech consumer products as well, and will until imports eventually comprise a majority of units shipped in Japan, the association said.

In 1996, Japan's entire production of electronics products grew an estimated 6.3 percent to 24.1 trillion yen, the EIAJ said. The growth was led primarily by strong demand for information and communications equipment, it said.
